title: Course final
cards/0/task: Walk through the turning-point years: 2002, 2004, 2014, 2016, 2020 and 2025.
cards/2/task: One shared library build for Revit 2024, Revit 2025, Unity and .NET 10.
cards/3/q: Why .NET Standard 2.1 rather than 2.0 for code shared by Unity and .NET 10?
cards/3/options/0: 2.1 has Span<T>, IAsyncEnumerable and default interface methods, and you do not need Framework here
cards/3/options/2: 2.0 is outdated and will not load
cards/3/explain: If you also need Framework, it is 2.0 or a separate net48 build.
cards/4/q: What is true in October 2026? Select all that apply.
cards/4/explain: Framework is frozen: .NET Standard 2.0 at most.
cards/5/q: Match each platform to its status
cards/5/pairs/3/1: Runtime of old Unity and Xamarin
cards/6/explain: Records came in C# 9, nullable in C# 8, async in C# 5.
cards/7/q: A plugin for Revit 2024 and Revit 2025
cards/8/q: What is the takeaway from the whole story?
cards/8/options/0: Code lives in the host's runtime: first find out where it will run, then pick the target
cards/8/explain: Revit, Unity and the server dictate the runtime. The TFM just answers them.
